test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 14 Oct, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Two trains are running in opposite directions at the same speed. The length of each train is 180 m. If they cross each other in 12 seconds, what is the speed of each train (in km/h)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In **opposite direction**, relative speed = sum of speeds.

Total Distance = Sum of lengths = 180 + 180 = 360 m.

Relative Speed = 360 m ÷ 12 sec = 30 m/s.

Since speeds are **equal**, speed of each train = 30 ÷ 2 = 15 m/s.

Speed in km/h = 15 × (18/5) = 54 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 54 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of each train (L₁ = L₂) = **180 m**

Time taken to cross each other (t) = **12 sec**

Speed of each train = **x m/s** (since they are equal)

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction) = (L₁ + L₂) ÷ Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4d3a2db717e87c4228ef1c4aa473d2bef1d7efd28eadadb0c1dc1f85c62bf01d.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative Speed = x + x = 2x

⇒ 2x = (180 + 180) ÷ 12

⇒ 2x = 360 ÷ 12

⇒ 2x = 30

⇒ x = 15 m/s

⇒ To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5:

⇒ Speed = 15 × (18 ÷ 5) km/h

⇒ Speed = 3 × 18 km/h

⇒ Speed = 54 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 54 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concepts

When moving in the **opposite direction**, Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂. When moving in the **same direction**, Relative Speed = |S₁ − S₂|.

Speed Unit Conversion

To convert **m/s to km/h**, multiply by 18/5. To convert **km/h to m/s**, multiply by 5/18.

Train Crossing Objects

Distance covered when crossing a **pole/man** = Length of train. Distance covered when crossing a **platform/bridge/another train** = Sum of lengths.</p
